purpose: Independent practice of B1.5 (even/odd) with reinforcement of B1.4 (skip-counting by 2s). Captures formative evidence on pair-up test, last-digit rule, and the skip-count connection.
student_learning_goal: I can describe what makes a number even or odd, and use the pair-up test to check.

header.student_learning_goal_banner: I can describe what makes a number even or odd, and use the pair-up test to check.
header.character_watermark: Detective Ona Ones in the top-right corner with a single '1' badge and a paper-clip evidence bag. Small (~1.5in tall).

parts.student_instructions: Each scene shows a small collection. Draw the pairing. Write EVEN or ODD.
parts.visual_layout: Top of the page. Six pair-up scenes in a 2x3 grid. Each scene shows a number of cubes (9, 12, 15, 18, 23, 26).

Each scene shows N small cubes scattered in a row with a blank pairing area below where the child will draw the pairing. Pre-fills: 9 cubes, 12 cubes, 15 cubes, 18 cubes, 23 cubes, 26 cubes. Below each scene, a label line for EVEN or ODD.

parts.answer_key: 9 ODD (4 pairs + 1). 12 EVEN (6 pairs). 15 ODD (7 pairs + 1). 18 EVEN (9 pairs). 23 ODD (11 pairs + 1). 26 EVEN (13 pairs).

parts.student_instructions: Circle the EVEN numbers. Underline the ODD numbers. Use the last-digit rule.
parts.visual_layout: Middle of the page. A 4x3 grid of 12 numbers. Each cell has a number in a light-grey outlined box.

parts.student_instructions: Three skip-count tasks. Fill in the missing numbers. The TRICKY one starts at 17 — what happens to the EVEN/ODD pattern?
parts.visual_layout: Bottom of the page. Three Number Line strips stacked. Strip 1: by 2s starting at 4 (to 30). Strip 2: by 2s starting at 17 (to 35) — TRICKY (lands on odds). Strip 3: by 2s starting at 100 (to 130).

early_finisher_prompt: If you finish, flip the page over. Pick a 3-digit number bigger than 200 and tell whether it's even or odd. How do you know without pairing up that many cubes?
teacher_notes: Lesson 3 consolidation. Hand out at the end of the Action phase. Watch for: (a) Part 1 children who can pair up cubes but get the EVEN/ODD label wrong — flag for the leftover-means-odd reteach; (b) Part 2 children who use majority-of-digits reasoning ('27 is even because 2 is even') — flag for the last-digit-rule reteach; (c) Part 3 Strip 2 children who fill in even numbers (16, 18, 20...) instead of odd (17, 19, 21...) — flag for the skip-count-from-odd-start practice.
